I need a sales page for my meal delivery service. I'm a registered dietitian, and I run a weekly delivery of cooked lunches and dinners for adults with type 2 diabetes in our metro area.

Facts:
- 10 meals a week cost $129, delivered every Sunday. A trial week costs $59.
- Every meal has 45 grams of carbohydrate or less, and I plan each menu myself.
- We have 88 active customers. 37 of them have been with us more than six months.
- 14 customers shared their A1C results with me from before they started and after three months. 10 went down, 3 stayed about the same, and 1 went up. The average drop was 0.6 points.
- I don't track whether customers changed their medication during that time.
- About 1 in 5 people who try a trial week sign up for the full plan.

I want the page to say our meals will lower your A1C. Around 400 words.

Before I write, there's one thing to settle, plus a few questions.

**The A1C claim.** I'd advise against saying the meals *will* lower someone's A1C, because your numbers don't back that up as a promise. Only 14 of your 88 customers shared results, and they chose to. One person's A1C went up. You also don't know who changed their medication during those three months. A skeptical reader, or a regulator looking at health claims, would spot that, and as a registered dietitian your credibility is the main thing you're selling. What the numbers do support is something like: *"Of 14 customers who shared their A1C with me before starting and after three months, 10 saw it go down, by an average of 0.6 points across all 14."* It's honest, specific and still persuasive. (Can you confirm whether the 0.6 average is across all 14 or only the 10 whose A1C dropped?)

My questions:

1. **Will you go with the honest version of the A1C result above instead of a promise?** If you'd like different wording, tell me what matters most to you.
2. **Who reads this page, and how do they get there?** Is it mostly the person with diabetes, or a spouse or adult child buying for them? Do they come from doctor referrals, search, ads or word of mouth?
3. **What do customers say about the food itself?** Do you have any quotes you're allowed to use, along with the cuisines or dishes people love most?
4. **What are the practical details?** I need the delivery area, the order cutoff, whether people can pause or cancel anytime, any options for allergies or vegetarians, and how the meals arrive and are reheated.
5. **What's your name, credential and business name, and what should the main button do?** For example: "Start a $59 trial week."

If you don't know something, say so and I'll leave it out rather than guess.

1. Yes, go with the honest version. I can't promise anyone's A1C will go down, and the meals don't replace their doctor's advice. On the 0.6, I'm not sure whether it's across all 14 or just the 10.
2. I don't know.
3. I don't have any quotes or know which dishes are favorites.
4. We deliver within 25 miles of downtown. Orders close Thursday at noon for that Sunday's delivery. The full plan has no contract, and customers can skip a week or cancel any time. I don't have specific allergy or vegetarian options, but customers can swap any meal for one of 6 other choices each week. I don't know how to describe the packaging or reheating.
5. Lena Ortiz, RD. The business is Steady Plate. The button should start a trial week.

I've written the page at about 400 words. I made three choices you should know about:

- **I left out the 0.6-point average.** If it's only the average of the 10 people whose A1C dropped, quoting it would make the results look better than they were. Once you know which group it covers, it can go back in. If it's across all 14, add: "On average across all 14, A1C dropped 0.6 points."
- **I left out the 1-in-5 trial conversion rate.** It doesn't help persuade anyone, and it doesn't need to be on the page.
- **I worked out the per-meal price ($12.90)** from your $129 for 10 meals. Delete it if you'd rather not show it.

# Steady Plate
## Lunches and dinners for type 2 diabetes, planned by a registered dietitian

Most people managing type 2 diabetes know what they're supposed to eat. The hard part is doing it every day: counting carbs, planning meals and cooking after a long day, week after week.

Steady Plate takes that work off your plate. Every Sunday, we deliver 10 cooked lunches and dinners to your door. Each one has **45 grams of carbohydrate or less**, so you don't have to count.

### Every menu is planned by a dietitian

I'm Lena Ortiz, a registered dietitian. I plan every Steady Plate menu myself. I don't use a template or an algorithm. I build each week's meals around the needs of adults living with type 2 diabetes.

### What our customers have seen

Fourteen customers shared their A1C results with me from before they started and after three months with us. **For 10 of them, A1C went down.** For 3 it stayed about the same, and for 1 it went up.

I'm sharing all of those numbers because I can't promise what will happen to your A1C. Everyone's body, medication and routine are different, and these 14 people chose to share their results. Steady Plate doesn't replace your doctor's advice or your treatment plan. It makes it easier to eat the way your care team recommends.

Today, 88 people get our meals each week. 37 of them have been with us for more than six months.

### How it works

- **10 meals a week for $129** (about $12.90 a meal), delivered every Sunday.
- **Change any meal you like.** Each week you can trade any meal for one of 6 other choices.
- **No contract.** Skip a week or cancel whenever you want.
- **Order by Thursday at noon** for that Sunday's delivery.
- **We deliver within 25 miles of downtown.**

### Try one week for $59

You don't need to commit to anything to find out whether Steady Plate works for you. A trial week costs $59. Eat the meals, see how they fit your days, and then decide.

**[Start my $59 trial week]**

*Steady Plate meals are not medical treatment and do not replace advice from your doctor or diabetes care team. Talk to your care team before changing your diet or medication.*

— Lena Ortiz, RD, founder of Steady Plate
